title: Movement of Robots
summary: Given an array of initial positions for robots on an infinite number line and a command direction ('L' for left or 'R' for right), calculate the sum of distances between all pairs of robots after d seconds, considering that robots reverse direction immediately upon collision.
statement: Given an array of initial positions for robots on an infinite number line and a command direction ('L' for left or 'R' for right), calculate the sum of distances between all pairs of robots after d seconds, considering that robots reverse direction immediately upon collision. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7. Note that pairs (i, j) and (j, i) are considered the same. Robots move one unit per second, and collisions occur when robots occupy the same position at the same time.
constraints: Robot i starts at nums[i] and moves left or right according to s[i], one unit per second for d seconds.
Robots pass through one another equivalently when they collide.
After d seconds, return the sum of distances over every unordered robot pair modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def sum_robot_distances(nums,s,d):
    MOD=1_000_000_007
    positions=sorted(value+(d if direction=='R' else -d) for value,direction in zip(nums,s))
    prefix=0;answer=0
    for index,value in enumerate(positions):answer=(answer+index*value-prefix)%MOD;prefix+=value
    return answer

hints: Collisions can be modeled as robots passing through because exchanging identities does not change the multiset of positions.
Compute every final position and sort them.
For sorted position x at index i, its distance to all earlier positions is i*x minus their prefix sum.
Sorting fixes every pair’s order, and the prefix formula counts each unordered pair exactly once.
